title: Compose the ordered setup command over the existing primitives
statement: Implement `bin/setup.mjs` running the ordered phases: path resolution, Node validation, the setup lock, the locked dependency install, the dynamic imports, the transaction plan, initialization, the project ID and state protection, the journal, trust, package registration, consent, model binding, credential contract, research choice, preflight, canary and read-back — with every installed dependency imported dynamically after the install step, and no second initializer.
notes:
⚠️ R9 IS SETUP'S (recorded 2026-09-13). The skill-override entry `../planning-content/skills-overrides` is fixed relative to `.pi`, while the content root can be selected elsewhere, for example through `PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR`. Setup owns making the entry it writes agree with the selected content root's `skills-overrides/`. TSK-0047 proves the entry only in the default layout, where the content root is `<project>/planning-content`.

⚠️ STAGE-DOCUMENT MIGRATION IS SETUP'S (recorded 2026-09-18, TSK-0049). `kiln_write_stage_document` writes into a `## Intake` section with two anchored regions, and refuses a document that does not have them rather than upgrading one during a write: a write is not the moment to restructure a document somebody may have edited. Projects initialized before that section existed therefore cannot record an answer until their stage documents carry it. Setup owns adding it, the same way it owns making the skill-override entry agree with the selected content root. Kiln's own Stage 1 document was migrated by hand as a one-off and is not the general answer.

⚠️ THE ORDER IS D26 (2026-09-22): paths, Node, lock, install, dynamic imports, plan, initializer, project ID and state protection, journal, then the remaining phases. The dependency install comes before the transaction plan because the plan validates existing Kiln records, and that validation needs Ajv, which the install is what provides. Everything up to and including the install is therefore built-ins only (ACC-0083), and the install is a bootstrap mutation confined to the .planning checkout: it changes no consumer project state and does not rewrite the lockfile. ⚠️ SLICE 1 LANDED 2026-09-22 (EVD-0133, commits e808b96 and 7ef9d4d). bin/setup.mjs runs D26's order as far as the journal: the five paths printed before any mutation, the engines check, the single lock held for the whole run, `npm ci --ignore-scripts` confined to this checkout, the dynamic imports, the transaction plan, and the phases state-coverage, initialize, state-protection and project-identity before the journal opens. Two review findings were closed in 7ef9d4d: the .gitignore fix now runs inside the planned transaction as a declared phase rather than before it, and the bootstrap install is locked and runs no dependency lifecycle script. ACC-0083 passes from that evidence. STILL OWED HERE: slice 2 (Pi import and version verification, trust, package registration, the skill-override entry agreeing with the selected content root — R9 above), slice 3 (consent, discovery, selection, the credential contract, research) and slice 4 (preflight, the live model check, read-back, the full exit-code mapping and resume), plus `--local-state user`, which refuses by name in slice 1. ACC-0085 waits until every supported state path is implemented; ACC-0043, ACC-0045, ACC-0106, ACC-0107 and ACC-0108 wait for the integration record after all slices land. ⚠️ REGISTRATION IS A PLANNED MERGE, NOT `pi install -l` (D27, 2026-09-22). Setup writes the package entry itself, through the transaction's own settings merge, and does not run `pi install -l` against the consumer project. `.pi/settings.json` is a planned target whose recorded identity is what makes the merge refuse a file that moved; `pi install -l` writes that file itself, so inside the plan it would have to be adopted — widening the rule that stops a concurrent edit being laundered into the plan — and outside the plan it would write a project file the transaction has not contained or probed. The portable entry `../.planning/pi-package` is written only after it is proved to resolve to this checkout's canonical package directory, and that the registered entry loads is proved by running pinned Pi against it. EVD-0079 and ACC-0105 remain the component proof of Pi's literal entry and its portable equivalent. Because the settings writer requires a provider, a model and a thinking level that are not chosen until slice 3, slice 2 writes through a package-and-skill-only merge that preserves existing defaults and every unrelated setting.
